articles.title: Claressa Shields not upset Katie Taylor fight didn't happen and sends retirement message to Irish great
articles.summary: Claressa Shields and Amanda Serrano both wished Katie Taylor a happy retirement as the Irish great prepares for the final bout of her professional career this weekend; Shields played down the idea she was upset the two never shared the ring, praising Taylor's historic career.
articles.body:
Taylor enters her farewell bout this weekend when she takes on Flora Pili in an undisputed super-lightweight world title clash at Dublin's Croke Park in front of more than 80,000 fans.

The Irish icon, a two-weight undisputed world champion and Olympic gold medallist, will hang up her gloves widely-recognised as the greatest fighter in female boxing history.

Five-weight world champion Shields has arguably become the closest rival to Taylor's reputation at the pinnacle of the sport.

"Am I number one? I have always shared that with Katie," Shields told Sky Sports. "Me and her joke and say we're 1A and 1B, because we're both just that good.

"I'm not a person that really cares about the pound for pound list. I know that I've been number one or two on there for the past five, six years.

"But I know that Katie, she's a great fighter. She's a warrior. And I wish her a happy retirement. And I hope that she gets a big knock out her last fight."

Shields, a three-time undisputed world champion, has fought at heavier weight-classes than Taylor, hence the pair never crossing paths in their respective glittering careers.

"I'm not mad that it didn't happen," said Shields. "We had weight classes for a reason. And I respect her greatness and she respects mine.

"I beat the best in my divisions, and she's beat the best in her divisions. I respect that. So no, I'm not upset that we never got to fight.

"I am happy to be able to watch her and her greatness. She's done the same for me. And like I said, I wish her a happy retirement."

Taylor enters Saturday's contest 25-1 having suffered her only professional career defeat against Chantelle Cameron in May 2023.

Among her highlights is a trilogy of wins over Puerto Rican great Amanda Serrano, the first of which saw the pair compete in the first ever women's boxing match to headline at Madison Square Garden.

"I think Katie's done what she wanted to do. I think this is her time," Serrano told Sky Sports.

"You can feel it, I've been 17 years in the sport. It's about time.

"Me and Katie, we've made lots of money together, we made history together and big fights. I think she's done enough for the sport. She deserves this homecoming fight.

"I'm happy for her. I just can't wait to see her future when she's retired with her family life and all that good stuff. She deserves it."

articles.title: Coach Hints at Islam Makhachev’s Potential UFC Return Date
articles.summary: American Kickboxing Academy head coach Javier Mendez hinted at when UFC welterweight champion Islam Makhachev will be ready to fight again.Makhachev is comin...
articles.body:
American Kickboxing Academy head coach Javier Mendez hinted at when UFC welterweight champion Islam Makhachev will be ready to fight again.

Makhachev is coming off a unanimous decision win over Ian Machado Garry at UFC 330 that saw him pick up his 17th win in a row, which is a UFC record.

That was Makhachev's only fight so far in 2026, but his coach says he might fight one more time before the year is up.

Islam Makhachev Could Return in December

Speaking on the "Weighing In" podcast, Mendez said that Makhachev could return tot the Octagon in December at UFC 335 if the promotion gives him enough notice so he can have a full two-month training camp.

"I think that he could be ready December on up potentiall. Potentially because I don't know exactly where his mind is at but one thing I do know, Islam's not gonna say no to any opponent. His only issue is going to be when do they want him to fight and that's it. The date (and) if he can have enough time because he always wants two months training camp. He's not going to take six weeks, seven weeks. Islam wants a two month training camp," Mendez said (via Bloody Elbow ).

As for who Makhachev will fight next, ultimately, it's the UFC's call who they will match him up against. But by all indications, it will be Carlos Prates, the Brazilian knockout artist who is confident that he can be the man who ends Makhachev's long UFC win streak.

If the UFC can get the fight booked, then Makhachev vs. Prates would be a terrific headliner for UFC 335, which takes place in December in Las Vegas.

There have been suggestions that UFC middleweight champion Sean Strickland could headline that card, but as of right now, Strickland has not been cleared to fight again following a shoulder injury he suffered before his fight against Khamzat Chimaev at UFC 328.

articles.title: UFC Champion Pulls Out Of UFC 332, Promotion Scrambles To Replace Main Event
articles.summary: Valentina Shevchenko is out of UFC 332 with an injury. Natalia Silva vs. Wang Cong for the interim flyweight title is reportedly being worked on for Oct. 3.
articles.body:
The UFC 332 has been thrown into a state of flux. UFC women's flyweight champion Valentina Shevchenko has been forced off the card with an injury. She was set to defend her 125-pound title against top contender Natalia Silva. With the champion out, the card's main event has been all but ruined. However, UFC brass is scrambling to find a replacement to ensure a title fight remains on the card. And they may have found a replacement for Shevchenko. Let's talk MMA.

Valentina Shevchenko vs. Natalia Silva, women's flyweight title

Shevchenko out with an undisclosed injury

Natalia Silva vs. Wang Cong, interim women's flyweight title

None. Dana White said the main event would be announced this week

Wang beat Shevchenko in a 2015 kickboxing bout

The injury report came from Brazilian outlet Ag. Fight , and the UFC has since removed Shevchenko vs. Silva from its website . Neither the promotion nor Shevchenko has commented publicly.

The interim booking traces to a single account on X and remains unannounced. UFC CEO Dana White said after Tuesday's Contender Series that the main event would be named this week.

Wang Cong has been on a roll with four straight wins after suffering the only loss of her MMA career to Gabriella Fernandes in November 2024. Most recently, Wang defeated Tracy Cortez via unanimous decision in July. The win pushed Wang to No. 6 in the flyweight division. Elevating her into a No. 1 contender or interim title fight with Silva makes sense. The other contenders ahead of Wang and behind Silva have either already had their shot at the title (Manon Fiorot, Alexa Grasso, Zhang Weili) or are sidelined and unavailable for the date (Erin Blanchfield).

For casual fans, Shevchenko-Silva was a weak main event on paper. Wang-Silva for an interim title reads even weaker to the average fan. The hardcores will still have some interest because the matchup still represents highly skilled, top-of-the-line mixed martial artists.

articles.title: Taylor-Pili: 'You couldn't make Katie Taylor's story up' - Eddie Hearn
articles.summary: Promoter Eddie Hearn says "the whole story, you couldn't make it up", when speaking of Katie Taylor's journey.
articles.body:
As promoter Eddie Hearn tries to quantify the impact Katie Taylor has made throughout her career, there is a smile and shake of the head as he says, "the whole story, you couldn't make it up."

On Saturday night, Taylor will make her final walk to the ring when she takes on Flora Pili at Croke Park, with the chance to become undisputed light-welterweight champion once again.

While Taylor entered professional boxing in 2016 with an Olympic gold medal, five world and seven European amateur titles to her name, there were no guarantees that star power could flourish in the paid code where women's boxing remained firmly in the shadows.

After agreeing to meet Taylor, her mother Bridget and manager Brian Peters, Hearn's interest was more than piqued.

"I went into that meeting, I would say 90% in my mind I wasn't going to do anything," said the Matchroom chairman.

"She's so fierce and the way she was talking, like the passion, the determination and she was telling me the story about the Olympics [pushing for women's boxing to be added to the programme for London 2012] and I was just like, 'this is unbelievable'. That was when we decided to headline her in November."

The decision to put Taylor on after Ohara Davies' victory over Andrea Scarpa that night at Wembley Arena was met with some scepticism from his father, Barry.

"He's like, 'oh, mate, no one's interested in the women's boxing' but he watched her debut and he was like, 'oh my God'.

"From there, the story's been unbelievable."

Taylor made around £6000 for that initial victory, "at the time in women's boxing, a lot of money" Hearn reflected, but that proved yet another obstacle Taylor was determined to overcome for female fighters.

Following a defence of the WBA and IBF light weight titles against Cindy Serrano - sister of great rival Amanda - at Boston's TD Garden in 2018, Taylor questioned why Tevin Farmer, who defended his IBF super-featherweight title against James Tennyson on the same card, made significantly more money.

"She said, 'do you think that's fair?', and I was like, 'no, but I just think that's the world and where we are right now'," Hearn recounted.

"She's like, 'well, how can I sell more tickets, how can more people be interested in me, how can more people want to tune in to watch me fight, yet he's making three times as much?'. I said, 'because he's a man and that's what you need to change'.

"Now she's making more than 99% of male fighters out there."

The three fights with Amanda Serrano, two at a sold-out Madison Square Garden and another on the Jake Paul-Mike Tyson card in Texas, have helped transform career earnings and raise the profile for women's boxing to heights many could not have envisaged.

While Taylor again pushed her promoter to seek a higher purse than the "incredible" offer made by Paul's MVP for that second meeting, Hearn accepts "she was right" and despite fighter and promoter not having a contract "for years and years", he can only conclude the Bray woman has been "incredible to work with".

The love and respect for the 40-year-old has been evident in the build-up to Saturday's last dance with contemporaries, former opponents and many more outside the boxing bubble lining up to show their appreciation for a career that has transformed the female fight game.

"Boxing is a really toxic world," Hearn accepts.

"There's always people who don't like people but there isn't one female fighter you could find that wouldn't go, 'she's incredible'.

"She's just so loved, there's no airs or graces. She's not there for the fame, she's not there for the money, it's purely her faith, the love of the sport and trying to set an example."
